generatedProse.concept-context: In practice, reflective practice runs across a whole degree, not once at the end of a single placement. After each experience you take it through the cycle, reflect honestly, and write down what you learned and will change. A short, honest round after each experience, with one change carried forward, is worth more than a long reflection written only when it is asked for.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two students each complete the same placement. One writes a tidy description of what the placement involved and leaves it there, treating the account as a one-off task. The other takes the experience through the cycle, reflects honestly on a moment that went wrong, links it to an idea from their course, and sets out what they will do differently next time. Over the year, the second student's accounts grow sharper, because reflection became a practice rather than a one-off.
generatedProse.summary: Reflecting on experience is most useful when it becomes one continuing practice. You run the cycle on each experience, reflect honestly, and articulate what you learned, again and again across your studies. It is the habit, not any single account, that turns experience into learning you can show.

check.body: A student finishes a placement, takes it through Kolb's cycle, reflects honestly on a session that went wrong, and writes an account showing what they now do differently. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following essay improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first essay, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next essay.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using feedback to plan the next piece of work feeds it straight back into your learning, closing the loop and starting the next round stronger. That is the cycle working as it should.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student did with the feedback, and what improved as a result.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Acting on feedback feeds your next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following essay was stronger. The mark on the first essay cannot change, but the feedback still shapes what comes next.

_items.text: That the three strands worked as one practice: the model, the reflection and the articulation together turned the placement into learning they can show.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three parts ran together on one experience, which is the whole practice.

_items.text: That only the parts of the placement that went wrong are worth reflecting on.
_items.feedback: Honest reflection covers what went well too, not only what went wrong.

_items.text: That the account is strong because it describes the placement in full detail.
_items.feedback: Description alone is not the point. The strength is the evidenced insight, not the detail of events.

_items.text: That the experience alone, once finished, counts as the learning.
_items.feedback: The experience is the occasion. The learning is what the student did with it through the practice.

_prompts.concept-context: What does this look like in practice within the given context? Write a short follow-on from the generic definition above, in the learner's own subject or discipline. Keep it to two or three sentences, mid-register, following straight on from the generic definition.
_prompts.worked-example: Give a subject-specific worked example of this lesson's concept: a weaker or less-developed version first, then a stronger version reached by better practice, using the context cast (character tokens) consistently. Keep the weaker-then-stronger shape and the two-part contrast; name the cast directly in the prose (the pack supplies the whole body). The merge renders it as a block quote, so write it as continuous prose, not as a quoted comment plus commentary.
_prompts.summary: Recap what the learner can now do, in terms of their own subject or context. One short paragraph. Do not restate the learning outcomes verbatim.
_prompts.check: Write the subject's own version of this lesson's check question(s), testing the same outcome in the learner's own discipline. Keep the same number of items and the same correctness pattern as the generic version; reword the stem and items for the subject. Keep the component-level feedback (correct / notFinal / final) teaching, never a bare verdict.
